newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS cargo not planning rate rise over surcharge.
newsitem.headline: SAS cargo not planning rate rise over surcharge.

text.p: Scandianvian airline SAS's cargo unit said on Wednesday it was not planning to replace its fuel surcharge with an increase of rates, following a similar move by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines KLM.

"We haven't decided to change our fuel surcharge. Until further notice we will continue with our fuel surcharge and monitor what else is happening on the market," Kim Moeller of SAS Cargo marketing told Reuters.
KLM said on December 17 it would raise air cargo rates by five to ten percent in the first quarter of 1997 and drop its present fuel surcharge at the same time.
Moeller said it made little difference for SAS whether it collected revenue from a fuel surcharge or by increasing rates.

"Basically it's still important for us to get this compensation as long as fuel prices are still as high as they are. Whether it is a fuel surcharge or a cargo rate increase is a secondary issue," he said.
He said SAS would leave cargo pricing as it was "so not to confuse the market further."

SAS said last month it would add a fuel surcharge to its cargo prices of between five and 10 U.S. cents. It would be specified on the airway bill as a charge called "due carrier" and would go to the airline to which the airway bill belonged.
